question.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Polar Curve Given the Derivatives With Respect To X and Y
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059545/assets/ab95faf73fa837d232a67a773afdbf456f5798d0f05de23e6ce44b41cddb1881.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the polar curve $r=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ (shown above) given that

$$
{y}^{′}(\theta )=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ we use the rule

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )} \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
